solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Loo? Gee, thanks — that's capital!

parts.note: bog is British slang for a toilet, as loo is
gee is an exclamation of surprise, as is 'O!' or 'oh'
ta is British informal for thank you

explanation.surface: Someone thrilled at being shown to the toilet exclaims gratefully that it's splendid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital!' reads as an old-fashioned cry of delight, but it is the definition, a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Bogotá is the seat of government of Colombia, its capital city.

clue.text: Eye Penny on a bicycle?

definitions.meaning: the London Eye is a giant observation wheel, a ferris-type ride
a penny-farthing bicycle has one huge front wheel, the 'penny', beside a small 'farthing'

explanation.surface: Someone sizes up a coin perched on a bike.
explanation.definitionFit: A big wheel is a fairground ferris wheel, like the London Eye, and literally the large front wheel of a penny-farthing; penny and farthing are old British coins.

clue.text: In old college Grieg's composed pastoral piece

indicators.note: composed means put together anew, so the letters are rearranged, apt for a composer

parts.note: OC is an abbreviation for old college
the composer's name with its S, taken as written

explanation.surface: At his former college, the Norwegian composer Grieg wrote a rustic work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' only joins: the letters of OC and GRIEGS together are shuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: Virgil's Georgics is a classical Latin poem about farming and rural life, a pastoral work.

clue.text: Wach over in days of yore?

parts.note: to watch over; take T, short for ...

explanation.surface: A misspelt 'watch over' asks whether guarding belonged to bygone days.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as an instruction: TIME (T) taken OUT OF MIND (watch over) leaves 'Wach over'.
explanation.definitionFit: Time out of mind means for longer than anyone can remember, i.e. back in the distant past.

clue.text: Like coteries possibly?

indicators.note: possibly signals that the word coteries may be rearranged into another form

explanation.surface: A question whether something resembles exclusive cliques.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: shuffle COTERIES, and the result describes what coteries are like.
explanation.definitionFit: Coteries are small exclusive circles whose interests are understood only by insiders, i.e. arcane and private.

clue.text: In succession, it's Queen badly needing friend

indicators.note: badly signals the preceding words are put together wrongly, so rearranged

parts.note: taken as its letters ITS, the apostrophe ignored
an ally is a friend or supporter

explanation.surface: One after another, a queen in trouble seeks a companion.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing things one after another in order is to do them in sequence.

clue.text: Until a depression he's on healthy-sounding grub

parts.note: to can mean until, as in nine to five
a dint is a dent or depression
taken as written

indicators.note: sounding marks that the healthy word is heard, not spelt

parts.note: whole means healthy, as in hale and whole

explanation.surface: Someone in a slump props himself up with wholesome food.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', a link meaning 'is placed on'. TOAD IN THE HOLE is a British dish of sausages baked in batter.
explanation.definitionFit: Grub is informal for food, and toad-in-the-hole is a hearty British dish.

clue.text: MP's daughter involved in review

indicators.note: involved in means wrapped up within, so the daughter's letter goes inside the review word

parts.note: a recap is a review or summary

explanation.surface: A Member of Parliament's daughter gets caught up in a review.
explanation.walkthrough: MP here is military police, not Member of Parliament; the 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Redcap is British slang for a military policeman, from the red cap covers they wear.

clue.text: US rivers have constant stink at start of summer

parts.note: C is the scientific symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light
to reek is to stink

indicators.note: at start of points to the opening letter of the word summer

explanation.surface: American waterways smell unchangingly foul as summer begins.
explanation.definitionFit: In American usage a creek is a small river or stream, not the tidal inlet the British word suggests.

clue.text: Opportunity among General Staff for Queen's officers

indicators.note: among puts the opportunity word between the letters of the staff abbreviation

parts.note: GS is the military abbreviation for General Staff
room means scope or opportunity, as in room for improvement

explanation.surface: A chance arises among senior military staff for officers serving the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Grooms of the royal household, such as Groom of the Stool, were officers serving the sovereign.

clue.text: Private quarter a dude is designing

indicators.note: designing means working into a new form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: Q is an abbreviation for quarter
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A trendy guy is planning private living quarters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Private' looks like an adjective for the quarters, but it is the army rank.
explanation.definitionFit: Squaddie is British slang for a private soldier, the lowest rank in the army.

clue.text: 'Ringer' vehicle ailing on climbing trip round head of Eskdale

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
ill means ailing

indicators.note: round means the reversed trip word goes around the next letter
climbing in a down clue means the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a run is a short trip, as in a run to the shops

indicators.note: head of points to the first letter of the word Eskdale

explanation.surface: A sick motorist sets off up the fells near Eskdale, a Lake District valley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ringer' suggests a lookalike or a fraudulent racehorse, but it is a bell-ringer.
explanation.definitionFit: A carillonneur plays a carillon, a set of tuned church bells, so is a bell ringer.

clue.text: Top achievement in advanced paper design

parts.note: high can mean advanced, as in high technology
a watermark is a faint design pressed into paper

explanation.surface: A designer's finest moment comes in advanced work on paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A high-water mark is the highest level reached, figuratively the peak of success.

clue.text: See 12
See 12
See 3
See 6
Racking collapses in exit, accruing …

indicators.note: collapses signals the following words fall apart and are reassembled

explanation.surface: An agonising moment as a building's exit falls in while debts mount up, leading into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Racking pain is torturing, as on the rack; excruciating pain is likewise agonising.

clue.text: Chinese perhaps worrying a lot about nothing in Senegal

indicators.note: about puts the jumbled letters around the French word
worrying means troubling or disturbing, so the letters are shaken up

parts.note: French is spoken in Senegal, and rien is French for nothing

explanation.surface: A Chinese person, perhaps, frets greatly over having nothing in West Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worrying' turns A LOT into OTAL, which 'about' wraps around; Senegal is French-speaking, which is why its word for nothing is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Oriental is a dated term for an Eastern Asian, of which a Chinese person is an example.

clue.text: Costa Rica and America raise revolutionary activist

parts.note: CR is the international code for Costa Rica
USA is the United States of America

indicators.note: raise in a down clue lifts the word up, so it reads backwards

parts.note: a red is a communist revolutionary

explanation.surface: Two American nations bring up a political insurgent.
explanation.definitionFit: A crusader campaigns vigorously for a cause, the very type of an activist.

clue.text: … initially tricky complication for Regal Hotel, needing early return for taxman

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of the word tricky
complication for signals that the pieces are tangled together and reordered

parts.note: the early part of return, its first letter R

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue, a tricky tax tangle for a grand hotel needs a prompt filing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needing' only joins; the opening ellipsis links back to 17 Across. 'complication for' rearranges REGAL HOTEL into OLLGATHERE.
explanation.definitionFit: A toll-gatherer collects charges for using a road or bridge, a kind of tax collector.

clue.text: Turn jeans up for wife to get into

indicators.note: to get into puts the wife's letter inside the reversed jeans word
up in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: Levi's is a well-known brand of jeans

explanation.surface: A husband rolls up his jeans so his wife can wriggle into them.
explanation.definitionFit: To swivel is to turn or pivot about a point.

clue.text: Problem of concentration with drink? Makes sense

parts.note: ADD is attention deficit disorder, a condition affecting concentration
to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: Does a concentration problem plus a drink seem logical?
explanation.definitionFit: When an explanation adds up it is consistent and believable, i.e. it is logical.

clue.text: Ladies' group joining churchman's Dales gathering learn 'Ecumenism for Beginners' — it offers a broader view

parts.note: the WI, Women's Institute, is a British women's organisation
a dean is a senior churchman; the 's is a link

indicators.note: gathering means taking in, so the valleys word goes around the first letters

parts.note: dales are valleys, as are glens

indicators.note: for Beginners means take the opening letters of learn and Ecumenism

explanation.surface: A Women's Institute branch joins a cleric's Yorkshire Dales meeting to study an introductory course on church unity.
explanation.definitionFit: A wide-angle lens captures a broader field of view than a standard camera lens.

clue.text: See 23
See 23
See 3

Suspicions when Nigel's stripped and in undies

indicators.note: in puts the stripped name inside the underwear word

parts.note: vests are British undershirts, worn as underwear

indicators.note: stripped means the outer letters are peeled off, leaving the middle of Nigel

explanation.surface: Suspicions arise when Nigel strips down to his underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Suspicion can mean a slight trace, as in a suspicion of garlic; vestiges are faint traces.

clue.text: Op-ed pieces about island race abridged

indicators.note: about puts the jumbled letters around the race
pieces means broken into bits, so the letters are reassembled

parts.note: the TT is the Tourist Trophy motorcycle race on the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: Opinion articles about an island motorcycle race are cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: A potted history is a condensed, shortened version, i.e. abridged.

clue.text: Trainee placing first of drones in beehive of stone

parts.note: L is for learner, from the L-plate on a learner driver's car

indicators.note: in puts that letter inside the beehive word

parts.note: an apiary is a place where bees are kept

indicators.note: first of points to the opening letter of the word drones

explanation.surface: An apprentice beekeeper puts the lead drone into a stone hive.
explanation.definitionFit: Lapidary relates to stones and gems and the cutting or engraving of them.

clue.text: Vault covers girl in credit

indicators.note: covers means the credit abbreviation wraps around the girl's name

parts.note: CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit
Ella is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A bank vault protects a young woman whose account is in credit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link: the credit letters cover ELLA.
explanation.definitionFit: A cellar is an underground storeroom, and a vault is an arched underground chamber.
